# Model Descriptives

## Variables of interest: SES, Neighborhood Insecurity and SDQ-Cas Total Difficulties

#### SES frequency table

```{r}
ses <-  bind_rows(
  full_panel %>%
    transmute(
      Wave = "2010",
      SES = estrato_2010
    ),
  full_panel %>%
    transmute(
      Wave = "2013",
      SES = estrato_2013
    ),
  full_panel %>%
    transmute(
      Wave = "2016",
      SES = estrato_2016
    )
)

ses_data_freq <- ses %>%
  group_by(Wave, SES) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Wave) %>%
  mutate(
    Percentage = round(100 * n / sum(n), 2)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()


ses_data_freq
```

#### SES distribution graph

```{r}
ggplot(ses_data_freq, aes(x = SES, y = n, fill = SES)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~ Wave) +
  labs(
    title = "Socioeconomic stratum distribution",
    x = "Socioeconomic stratum",
    y = "N"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

#### Descriptives for socioeconomic stratum 2010 x neighborhood violence x SDQ-Cas total difficulties

```{r}
model_data <-  bind_rows(

      SES = estrato_2010,

)


model_data_freq <- model_data %>%
  group_by(SES, Wave, Insecurity) %>%
```

## Pure predictor and base confounders (C0) vs. Exposure

List of possible baseline confounders:

- Richness tertile

- Whether mother lives with the child (C0 and Lt)

- Whether father lives with the child (C0 and Lt)

- mother's civil status (C0 and Lt)

- mother's employment status (C0 and Lt)

- Mother's educational attainment (C0)

- Ethnicity (C0)

- Age (C0)

- Region (C0)

- Sex (C0)

#### Richness tertile vs. SES

When observing the frequency tables, we can see that both measurements seem to be increasing and decreasing at similar capacities. Therefore, we can assume that SES effectively captures family level SES as well as neighborhood SES.

```{r}

table (full_panel$estrato_2010, full_panel$tercil_2010)

table (full_panel$estrato_2010, full_panel$tercil_2013)

table (full_panel$estrato_2010, full_panel$tercil_2016)
```

#### Age

```{r}

age_stratum_data <- bind_rows(
  full_panel %>%
    transmute(
      Wave = "2010",
      SES = estrato_2010,
      Age = edad_2010
    ),
  full_panel %>%
    transmute(
      Wave = "2013",
      SES = estrato_2010,
      Age = edad_2013
    ),
  full_panel %>%
    transmute(
      Wave = "2016",
      SES = estrato_2010,
      Age = edad_2016
    )
) %>%
  filter(!is.na(SES), !is.na(Age)) %>%
  mutate(
    Wave = factor(Wave, levels = c("2010", "2013", "2016")),
    SES = factor(SES)
  )

age_stratum_desc <- age_stratum_data %>%
  group_by(Wave, SES) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    Mean = mean (Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    SD = sd (Age, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Wave) %>%
  mutate(
    Percentage = round(100 * n / sum(n), 2)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

age_stratum_desc

```

## Time varying and intermediate confounders (Lt)

Variables that we assume are consequence of the exposure and base confounders and affect the mediators and outcomes.

#### Number of people living in the household

Frequency table for number of people living in household per stratum

```{r}
people_stratum_data <- bind_rows(
  full_panel %>%
    transmute(
      Wave = "2013",
      SES = estrato_2010,
      N = t_personas_2013
    ),
  full_panel %>%
    transmute(
      Wave = "2016",
      SES = estrato_2010,
      N = t_personas_2016
    )
)%>%
  filter(!is.na(SES), !is.na(N)) %>%
  mutate(
    Wave = factor(Wave, levels = c("2013", "2016")),
    SES = factor(SES)
  )

people_stratum_freq <- people_stratum_data %>%
  group_by(Wave, SES) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    Mean = mean (N, na.rm = TRUE), 
    SD = sd (N, na.rm = TRUE),
    Min = min(N),
    Max = max(N),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Wave) %>%
  mutate(
    Percentage = round(100 * n / sum(n), 2)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

people_stratum_freq
```

Graph for number of people in the household per socioeconomic stratum

```{r}
ggplot(people_stratum_data, aes(x = SES, y = N, fill = SES)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ Wave) +
  labs(
    title = "Total people in household distribution by socioeconomic stratum",
    x = "Socioeconomic stratum",
    y = "N"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
```

#### Child's studying status

